findings.title: Removing the Context copy constructor breaks existing grant providers
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` was removed rather than deprecated. This is a public nested type in the grant SPI, so external grant implementations compiled against the previous server SPI that clone their context will fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError`; source consumers also no longer compile. Retain the constructor (including the new `grantType` field) to preserve provider compatibility.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the fixed two-character encoding
findings.body: The encoder/parser protocol assumes exactly two characters for every grant shortcut: encoding concatenates the shortcut into a six-character prefix, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix whose length is not six. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` has no two-character constraint (its documentation even says shortcuts are usually three letters), and this factory stores custom shortcuts unchanged. A custom grant returning `foo` will successfully issue IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, but those IDs cannot be decoded and will throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate shortcut length/format and uniqueness at registration, or make the wire format length-delimited.

findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: The fourth null check checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw token ID can be constructed despite the error message and apparent invariant; the default encoder then serializes it as the literal string `null`. Check `rawTokenId` here so malformed contexts fail at construction.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: The matcher extracts `substring(3, 5)`, but in the six-character prefix the grant shortcut is at indexes 4 and 5 (`substring(4, 6)`). It also returns `false` when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For normal expected shortcuts such as `ac`, `rt`, `dg`, and `ci`, the condition is false and the matcher accepts any six-character context prefix as long as the suffix is a UUID. Thus the updated integration assertions do not test that the emitted grant encoding is correct. Require a six-character prefix and return the equality comparison for `substring(4, 6)`.
